title: 5,000-Year-Old Cuneiform Tablet With a Seal Signature
description:
Five thousand years ago, someone rolled a carved stone seal across wet clay to vouch for what was probably a barley record. The stone seems lost, but its signature (a man leading dogs after wild boars) survives on this Mesopotamian tablet, among the earliest writing known.

Sources:
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, proto-cuneiform tablet with seal impressions, accession 1988.433.1, ca. 3100-2900 BCE (Jemdet Nasr period; date approximate), probably from Uruk, Mesopotamia. metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/329081
The Met, "The Origins of Writing" (essay)
The Met, "Cylinder Seals: Tiny Treasures That Leave a Big Impression"
CDLI P005393
Britannica, "cylinder seal"
Unicode proposal L2/19-284 (proto-cuneiform)
Antiquity (2024), "Rolling back the origins of writing"
The reading as a barley handout is the Met's (early texts have no verbs, so it is uncertain); per the Met, the seal itself apparently has not survived.

Visuals: The Met 3D scan of 1988.433.1 (CC0), rendered in Blender; lighting: Poly Haven studio_small_09 (CC0). Narration voice is synthetic.
